subject: Proposal: p50/p95 quantile adjustment & rolling-window carveout for Hosted API
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Caldwell <ethan.caldwell@quantahealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-28T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: p50/p95 quantile adjustment & rolling-window carveout for Hosted API

Ethan — attaching an updated SLO proposal after our call this morning. Key asks and rationale are summarized below; full details are in the attached PDF and the CSV shows sample measurement windows from our telemetry.

Summary of proposal (short):
- Commitments: p50 = 40 ms, p95 = 200 ms for the Hosted API in the US region (measured on production traffic).
- Measurement: 5-minute rolling quantiles sampled at 1-minute intervals; 24-hour aggregation for reporting and billing.
- Burst carveout: transient bursts that exceed 10x baseline QPS sustained < 90 seconds are excluded from p95 calculations for that 5-minute window, provided the customer uses our recommended prefix caching settings.
- Regional fallback: if US region is degraded and traffic automatically routes to EU/zone fallback for < 30 minutes, those routed requests will be considered in a separate regional bucket and not penalize the US commitment if capacity failure is demonstrated.

Rationale: our telemetry shows that tail spikes are often caused by short-lived fanout patterns (cron bursts, nightly batch retries) that distort rolling quantiles. The burst carveout keeps incentives aligned — we still guarantee expected performance for steady-state user traffic while recognizing ephemeral load patterns.

Requested next steps:
1) Please confirm whether the 5-minute rolling window and the 90-second burst carveout would be acceptable to QuantaHealth procurement.
2) If accepted, we will add the clause to the SOW and run a 14-day canary with your staging traffic (no billing changes during canary).
3) We can include a short audit report (sampled minute-level histograms) at the end of canary to validate measurements.

Attachments: hosted-slo-proposal-v2.pdf (proposal text + example SLAs), measurement-window-examples.csv (sample telemetry slices).

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
D: +1 415 555 0129
https://redwood.ai/
From: Ethan Caldwell <ethan.caldwell@quantahealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: QuantaHealth Procurement <procurement@quantahealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: p50/p95 quantile adjustment & rolling-window carveout for Hosted API

Diego — thanks for the clear write-up. A few quick clarifying Qs from Procurement and SRE: 

1) The p95 = 200 ms number is reasonable for our interactive UIs, but our batch inference paths need a tighter bound on median latency. Can we make the p50 commitment conditional on request type (interactive vs batch)?
2) For the burst carveout, how do you define "baseline" QPS? Is it rolling average over 1 hour or a fixed contract baseline?
3) The regional fallback language is important — we need an objective test to demonstrate "capacity failure" (e.g. 3 consecutive 1-minute windows where availability < 95% in the primary region).

Also please confirm that the canary will not count against our committed usage during the 14 days. Procurement wants to see the canary telemetry before signing.

Ethan
Senior Cloud Architect, QuantaHealth
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Caldwell <ethan.caldwell@quantahealth.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-29T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: p50/p95 quantile adjustment & rolling-window carveout for Hosted API

Ethan — thanks for the questions. Quick answers and an adjusted proposal below.

1) Conditional medians: we can tier p50 commitments by route-class. Suggested wording: interactive endpoints (route prefix /v1/chat or requests using streaming) commit to p50 = 40 ms; non-interactive batch endpoints commit to p50 = 120 ms. We will let you map your endpoints to route-classes during the canary.

2) Baseline QPS definition: baseline = 1-hour rolling median QPS sampled every 5 minutes. Carveout triggers if observed QPS in a 1-minute sample >= 10x baseline AND the 5-minute rolling quantile for that window exceeds the p95 threshold; transient carveouts apply only to the affected 5-minute window. We recorded examples in the CSV attachment.

3) Capacity failure objective test: agreed to your suggestion — primary region considered degraded if three consecutive 1-minute windows show 95% availability or lower for the configured model endpoint. If that occurs and traffic is routed to fallback region, requests handled by fallback for the duration of the incident will be evaluated separately from the primary-region SLA.

Canary: Redwood will not bill QuantaHealth for requests routed to special canary capacity during the 14-day evaluation. Post-canary, we will present minute-level histograms for a 7-day snapshot as an audit artifact.

If that all sounds good, Diego and I will produce SOW language and a short confirmation call can nail down endpoints.

—Aditya
VP, Product & Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Caldwell <ethan.caldwell@quantahealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, QuantaHealth Procurement <procurement@quantahealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: p50/p95 quantile adjustment & rolling-window carveout for Hosted API

Ethan / Procurement team — great, thanks for the fast feedback. Per Aditya's adjustments, we've updated the proposal and attached the SOW excerpt that would be added to the Master Services Agreement. Next practical steps:

1) Procurement: review the attached SOW excerpt (hosted-slo-proposal-v2.pdf) and confirm any remaining redlines.
2) SRE / Tech: if you can send example endpoint prefixes for mapping to route-classes we will pre-configure canary routing.
3) Schedule: propose a short 30-minute call on Monday (2027-06-02) to finalize endpoint mapping and authorize the canary.

If Procurement approves the language, we will add a clause that explicitly states the 90-second transient-burst carveout behavior and the measurement definitions Aditya listed (baseline = 1-hr rolling median; 5-min rolling quantiles sampled every minute).

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Diego.Fernandez@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0129
thread_summary: Sales thread negotiating p50/p95 commitments for Hosted API. Redwood proposes 5-minute rolling quantiles with a 90-second transient-burst carveout and regional fallback handling. QuantaHealth requests clarifications on conditional medians, baseline definition, and objective failure tests. Redwood agrees to conditional route-class p50s, defines baseline as 1-hour rolling median, and confirms canary will be non-billable.
notes: This thread will be used to update the SOW; attachments include a PDF SOW excerpt and telemetry CSV. Internal participants are members of sales and product leadership. External contact is QuantaHealth procurement/architecture.
